title: SeDeM: Selective Decompression of Hidden-State Memories for Long-Context Question Answering
event_hint: SeDeM: a long-context QA framework that stores context as compressed hidden-state memory blocks, selects query-relevant blocks, and decompresses only those into a decoder layer, beating compression baselines and, with a 3B backbone, exceeding full-context fine-tuning on three of four datasets while lowering TTFT vs ICAE.
problem: Long-context inference is costly: prefill self-attention scales quadratically with sequence length and the KV cache grows with processed tokens, while larger context windows do not guarantee reliable evidence use. Existing soft-compression methods use an LLM as compressor and rely on compact memory tokens both to preserve information and to condition the decoder, coupling storage and decoding.
mechanism: SeDeM decouples compact memory storage from decoder conditioning. A frozen LLM extracts hidden states from a chosen intermediate Transformer layer; a lightweight compressor stores each segment as a memory block; a query-conditioned selector (trained with block-level evidence supervision) picks relevant blocks; a decompressor expands only the selected blocks into hidden states compatible with an intermediate decoder layer. The decoder thus avoids both full-context processing and direct generation from highly compressed slots. Because memory construction is query-independent, memories are reusable across queries and support cross-model (small encoder, larger decoder) use.

evidence.claim: On four long-context QA benchmarks SeDeM beats the evaluated compression baselines in both 1B and 3B same-backbone settings; with the 3B backbone it exceeds full-context fine-tuning on three datasets (2WikiMultiHopQA, QASPER, HotpotQA-Distractor).
evidence.value: 3B SeDeM > full-context FT on 3 of 4 datasets
evidence.baseline: LongLLMLingua, HMT, ICAE, 500x, Activation Beacon; full-context fine-tuning reference

evidence.claim: Concrete 3B F1 scores: 2WikiMultiHopQA 67.25 (SeDeM) vs 62.50 (full-context FT) and 38.77 (ICAE); HotpotQA-Distractor 58.30 vs 36.73 (full-context FT); on MuSiQue SeDeM (21.85) remains below full-context FT (32.54).

SeDeM reduces online time-to-first-token versus ICAE: averaged across the four datasets, 3B TTFT is 79.60 ms vs 195.76 ms (2.46x), and 1B TTFT is 46.56 ms vs 81.07 ms (1.74x); on QASPER 3B the speedup reaches 3.77x (96.50 ms vs 364.10 ms).
evidence.condition: Fully online protocol (includes compression, selection, decoder prefill)

evidence.claim: SeDeM also improves autoregressive decoding throughput versus ICAE: 3B avg 45.16 vs 41.17 Tok/s (1.10x) and 1B avg 77.78 vs 71.82 Tok/s (1.08x); early-exit query encoding reduces 3B selection latency from ~26 ms to ~13 ms.
SeDeM's added inference-active modules are 33.59M params (2.72% of the frozen 1B backbone) and 75.55M params (2.35% of the 3B backbone), excluding LoRA adapters.

evaluation_context: Four long-context QA benchmarks: 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, QASPER, HotpotQA-Distractor (train/val splits reported in Table 7). Backbones Llama-3.2-1B-Base and 3B-Base (frozen + LoRA). Baselines: LongLLMLingua (hard), HMT/ICAE/500x (soft), Activation Beacon (KV/activation), plus frozen and full-context fine-tuned references. Metrics: token-level F1 and ROUGE-L. Efficiency measured by TTFT (ms) and throughput (Tok/s) under a fully online protocol. A cross-model row uses a 1B encoder with a 3B decoder (e.g., HotpotQA F1 44.39).
limitations: Explicitly stated by the authors: (1) the selector needs block-level evidence labels for training (all four benchmarks provide them); without labels, selector-disabled mode forgoes the efficiency gains of top-K selection. (2) Only Llama-3.2-1B and 3B are evaluated; transfer to substantially larger backbones is unverified. (3) Extraction and injection layers are chosen empirically, with no principled procedure for new backbone families. (4) With 3B, SeDeM stays below full-context FT on MuSiQue, and the selection budget K trades quality against context/efficiency. (5) Latency follows a fully online protocol; precomputing query-independent memories could improve efficiency but is not evaluated.
project_relevance: Relevant to compression/transfer/placement. SeDeM's query-independent memory construction makes compressed context reusable across multiple queries over the same context, and its selective decompression reduces both decode cost and TTFT. For cross-region or cross-session reuse, storing compact hidden-state memory blocks (rather than full KV) could lower bandwidth and storage cost while preserving QA quality, with the caveat that selection currently relies on evidence labels.
